section_summary: These pages document Japanese party politics, labor unrest, elections, and occupation policy in early 1947. State Department correspondence forwards SCAP interviews and analyses of coalition negotiations, party organization, and electoral plans, alongside British parliamentary exchanges and Soviet press reporting. The section also includes reports on Japanese nationalism and wartime politics, the Allied Council’s discussion of a general election, and changes to the House of Representatives election law.

subfiles.title: Transmitting “The Anti-Government Movement”
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards P. K. Roest’s report on the opposition movement.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch forwarding the SCAP report.

subfiles.title: The Anti-Government Movement
subfiles.about: Assesses the opposition’s dissolution motion, possible coalition cabinet, and merger talks.
subfiles.summary: Roest argues that the dissolution motion helped Socialists press Yoshida while preserving prospects for cooperation. He lists possible ministers and describes negotiations among smaller centrist parties.

subfiles.title: Control of Social Democratic Party of Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports concern that a purge of Nishio and Hirano could shift Socialist control leftward.
subfiles.summary: Quotes an intelligence summary on Socialist leadership, coalition negotiations, and possible elections.

subfiles.title: Current Japanese Political Situation
subfiles.to: Mr. Penfield; Mr. Borton; Mr. Allison; Mr. Emmerson
subfiles.about: Reviews the economic crisis, threatened strike, and stalled coalition negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Fearey connects workers’ hardship and the planned February strike to declining support for the Yoshida government. He examines Socialist demands for economic ministries, the dispute over Ishibashi, and prospects for a coalition.

subfiles.title: House of Commons questions on Japan
subfiles.about: Relays parliamentary questions on local purges, municipal elections, and broadcasting control.
subfiles.summary: British ministers discuss candidate screening and election delays, while affirming support for continued state control of Japanese broadcasting.

subfiles.title: DC/R routing slip
subfiles.about: Routes copies of the preceding communication.
subfiles.summary: Internal distribution slip.

subfiles.title: Komsomol Pravda article on Japanese youth
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Soviet article on Japan’s Communist youth movement.
subfiles.summary: The article describes youth organizing, cooperation with labor and peasant groups, political education, and clashes with nationalist youth.

subfiles.title: Soviet article on the situation in Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes A. Sibiryakov’s criticism of Yoshida and the Socialist right wing.
subfiles.summary: The article presents opposition to Yoshida as widespread, criticizes coalition tactics, and attacks the ban on a general strike.

subfiles.title: Pravda commentary on Japanese political crisis
subfiles.about: Relays Soviet criticism of Yoshida’s policies and cabinet changes.
subfiles.summary: Pravda portrays agrarian reform and democratization as inadequate and calls for a government representing the opposition, including Communists.

subfiles.title: Brumbaugh letter forwarding university report
subfiles.about: Offers copies of a report on his Japan trip and a proposed Christian university.
subfiles.summary: Brumbaugh asks that Schuler receive a copy and thanks Borton for assisting his trip.

subfiles.title: Reply to Brumbaugh
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the promised report and agrees to pass a copy to Schuler.
subfiles.summary: Allison thanks Brumbaugh for making the documents available.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Times comment on Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Times editorial advocating an early Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch summarizing the clipping’s call for an early treaty.

subfiles.title: Changing Japan, first clipping
subfiles.about: Argues for an early peace settlement to encourage democratic responsibility in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Editorial discusses British and Australian interests, democratic habits, occupation, and the timing of peace terms.

subfiles.title: Changing Japan, duplicate clipping
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the editorial on Japanese democracy and peace terms.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate clipping of the Times editorial.

subfiles.title: Pravda article on Japan’s internal politics
subfiles.about: Summarizes M. Merkov’s criticism of MacArthur’s election rationale and Yoshida’s government.
subfiles.summary: Merkov claims economic and political power remains undemocratic despite proposed elections.

subfiles.title: Transmitting memorandum on the anti-government movement
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a recently obtained December 1946 memorandum on opposition parties.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for Roest’s anti-government movement memorandum.

subfiles.title: The Anti-Government Movement, second copy
subfiles.about: Reproduces the earlier analysis of the dissolution motion, cabinet possibilities, and centrist merger.
subfiles.summary: This clearer copy repeats the memorandum on Socialist tactics and a proposed coalition cabinet. It also details talks to combine Co-operative Democrats and the People’s Party.

subfiles.title: Interview with Nozaka Sanzo: covering assessment
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs colleagues
subfiles.about: Recommends the attached Nozaka interview and compares it with earlier conversations.
subfiles.summary: Emmerson emphasizes Nozaka’s consistent staged approach to democracy, socialism, and communism.

subfiles.title: File note on Inukai and Nozaka interviews
subfiles.about: Recommends reading the enclosed interviews, especially Nozaka’s account of Communist plans.
subfiles.summary: Brief appraisal of the two interview memoranda.

subfiles.title: Organization and Plans of the Progressive and Communist Parties
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP interviews with Ken Inukai and Sanzo Nozaka.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch identifying two enclosed party interviews.

subfiles.title: Interview with Inukai Ken
subfiles.about: Records Inukai’s views on Progressive Party organization, elections, finances, and mergers.
subfiles.summary: Inukai discusses party factions, relations with Liberals, candidates, and campaign financing. Roest concludes that party management remains dominated by its leaders despite talk of reform.

subfiles.title: Interview with Sanzo Nozaka
subfiles.about: Records Nozaka’s Communist platform, political strategy, foreign relations, and electoral plans.
subfiles.summary: Nozaka proposes further purges, administrative reform, land reform, and national control of major industries as steps toward socialism. He distinguishes Communist mass action from Socialist parliamentary methods and denies current Soviet assistance. The interview also records candidate plans, funding needs, and expected electoral strengths by prefecture.

subfiles.title: Daily report on rice deliveries
subfiles.about: Reports Ritsu Ito’s charge that low government rice prices delay deliveries.
subfiles.summary: Ito calls the purchase price of 550 yen per koku unreasonable.

subfiles.title: Transmitting memorandum on recent political developments
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP memorandum on opposition activity and coalition talks.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for Roest’s February political assessment.

subfiles.title: Recent Political Developments
subfiles.about: Analyzes the failed coalition negotiations and their effect on Japanese parties.
subfiles.summary: Despite difficult OCR, the memorandum describes Socialist withdrawal from coalition talks, disputes over Ishibashi and financial policy, and factional maneuvering among Progressives and Socialists. It predicts political gains for the Socialists.

subfiles.title: File note on The Brocade Banner
subfiles.about: Describes an enclosed historical report on Japanese officers’ insurrectionary movements.
subfiles.summary: Notes its use of police and court records and highlights the Mazaki and Nagata episode.

subfiles.title: Transmitting The Brocade Banner, original
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a special report on Japanese nationalism based on police and court records.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for five copies of The Brocade Banner.

subfiles.title: Transmitting The Brocade Banner, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the despatch forwarding The Brocade Banner.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover despatch.

subfiles.title: Transmitting The Brocade Banner, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the despatch forwarding The Brocade Banner.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover despatch.

subfiles.title: Izvestia on pre-election maneuvering
subfiles.about: Summarizes Soviet allegations of bribery, eased purges, and reactionary election-law changes.
subfiles.summary: Izvestia attacks Yoshida’s supporters and the proposed replacement of plural voting.

subfiles.title: File note on War Politics in Japan
subfiles.about: Describes a SCAP report on wartime political associations and their membership.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the report questions early occupation assumptions about association membership.

subfiles.title: Transmitting War Politics in Japan, original
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards five copies of the August 1946 report War Politics in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for a Civil Intelligence Section report.

subfiles.title: Transmitting War Politics in Japan, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the despatch forwarding War Politics in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover despatch.

subfiles.title: Transmitting War Politics in Japan, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the despatch forwarding War Politics in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover despatch.

subfiles.title: Special Allied Council meeting concerning general election
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a record of MacArthur’s consultation with Allied Council members.
subfiles.summary: States that no member objected to the proposed election letter.

subfiles.title: Meeting of General MacArthur with Allied Council members
subfiles.about: Records unanimous Allied Council support for MacArthur’s letter calling for a Japanese general election.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur reads his proposed instruction to Yoshida and explains that a new Diet should coincide with the new constitution. Council members agree; Derevyanko briefly asks for more time to consider details.

subfiles.title: Forwarding three election memoranda
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards memoranda on two parties and Tokyo metropolitan elections.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch identifying three enclosed SCAP memoranda.

subfiles.title: Japan Farmers’ Party interview
subfiles.about: Questions Masakiyo Kita about the party’s purpose and prospects amid pending purges.
subfiles.summary: Kita says the party seeks to organize farmers despite likely disqualification of most founders. Roest doubts the small party will have political influence.

subfiles.title: The People’s Co-operative Party
subfiles.about: Documents the party merger, officers, ideology, finances, and election preparations.
subfiles.summary: Miki and Matsumoto describe the merger that formed the People’s Co-operative Party and its plans to field candidates. The memorandum lists party officers and examines its centrist, co-operative program. It also covers campaign funding, candidate support, and the search for a president.

subfiles.title: Tokyo-to Elections
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo electoral offices, registration, and polling-place expansion.
subfiles.summary: Reports voter counts, ward changes, a special registration period, and plans for more polling places.

subfiles.title: Forwarding SCAP message on election law
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s response concerning the House of Representatives election law.
subfiles.summary: Requests distribution of the enclosed message to commission members.

subfiles.title: SCAP message on House election law, surviving page
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Describes franchise rules and major amendments to the House election law.
subfiles.summary: Lists new districts, election committees, higher deposits and fines, a single ballot, and campaign restrictions.

subfiles.title: Request for consultation concerning House election law
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP’s response to a Far Eastern Commission consultation request.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of the enclosed SCAP message to the U.S. commission representative.
